title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review initial benchmark results from Redwood Dedicated pilot, confirm customer access and VPC peering status, discuss tuning knobs for latency vs cost, and agree next steps for security documentation and follow-up benchmarks.
action_items: Owner: Jenna Cho; Item: Run 5k-request throughput benchmark with optimized batching and 8-bit quantization, include token-level cost estimate; Due: 2027-10-19
Owner: Liam O'Connor; Item: Confirm VPC peering details and provide subnet/CIDR and firewall rules by email; Due: 2027-10-15
Owner: Samir Patel; Item: Share SOC 2 summary, KMS integration guide, and a short security deck; Due: 2027-10-14
Owner: Priya Nair; Item: Provide final pilot success criteria and SLA expectations (latency P50/P95 targets, max cost per 1k requests); Due: 2027-10-20
next_steps: Redwood to run tuned benchmark and share results sheet
Customer to complete VPC peering and provide KMS keys for test environment
Redwood to send security docs (SOC 2 summary, audit log example, RBAC notes)
Set follow-up check-in: 2027-10-19 10:00 PT to review benchmark outputs
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-10-12 15:00 PT | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Priya (NexaHead), Liam (Nexa SRE), Marta (Nexa Compliance)
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, quick agenda — onboarding status, results from last week's run, tuning, and open security items.
[00:22] Priya: yep thanks Samir, excited to see the numbers. we're a bit delayed on the VPC peering but Liam's on the call to, um, give an update.
[00:35] Liam: yeah, short update — I tried the peering template you sent, a couple ip ranges clash with our prod, so I'm going to adjust and share our subnet list later today.
[01:10] Jenna: cool, that matches what we expected — on the Redwood side we've provisioned a dedicated pool for the pilot, and we've enabled KV caching for the workload you shared.
[01:40] Marta: quick security question, is the KMS integration in place for logs/encryption or is that next step?
[01:55] Samir: KMS is optional in the pilot right now, currently using customer-managed keys is supported; Jenna will walk through the KMS flow.
[02:10] Jenna: yeah so for the test env we can either use our test key or you can bring your KMS. for production you'd definitely bring your key — we have a guide. I'll send it after call.
[03:05] Samir: ok results — Jenna, can you give us the baseline numbers we ran on Tuesday?
[03:20] Jenna: sure. so baseline was the model xlarge-v2, unquantized, small batch size 4, median latency around 210ms per request at p50, p95 about 870ms, throughput about 180 req/min on the current Dedicated node. transcription had some dropped tokens in the longer context runs, probably due to batching fall-through.
[04:02] Priya: 870ms p95 is a bit high for our interactive use case — what tuning knobs do you recommend?
[04:18] Jenna: main levers: increase batching to improve throughput/cost, but that can add latency; enable 8-bit quantization with the quant profile we shipped — that dropped p95 to ~420ms in our lab runs; also aggressive KV cache for prefixes reduces repeated token compute.
[04:45] Liam: what about the cost delta when you quantize? we care about accuracy loss.
[04:55] Jenna: good question — in our evals 8-bit quantization had minimal semantic degradation on your chat prompts, accuracy drop under 1.5% on intent classification tests. cost per token reduced roughly 35%.
[05:25] Priya: ok can you run the quantized run against our 5k sample requests?
[05:35] Jenna: yes we'll do a 5k run with batching 8 and quantization, plus one with batching 2 and no quant to compare.
[06:00] Marta: about audit logs — do they include token-level traces or just request metadata?
[06:12] Samir: we capture request/response metadata, timestamps, model version, route, but by default not full token payloads for privacy — we can turn on more verbose logging for debugging if you want.
[06:40] Marta: we'll need examples for our auditor — can you send sanitized log snippets?
[06:50] Samir: yes, will include sanitized examples in the security pack.
[07:20] Jenna: quick note on fallback policies — if your Dedicated pool hits capacity we can auto-route to a compatible hosted variant to avoid errors, there is config to control that.
[07:50] Liam: is that auto-route encrypted across VPCs? we need to ensure in-flight encryption and don't want data leaving our region.
[08:05] Samir: all traffic uses TLS; for region constraints we can pin region and disable cross-region fallback for the pilot.
[08:30] Priya: timeline check — our goal is to complete environment readiness and run conclusive benchmarks by end of next week. is that feasible?
[08:45] Jenna: yes — if peering and KMS are done early next week we can schedule the 5k run Tues/Wed.
[09:12] Samir: let's talk about success criteria — Priya, you mentioned interactive latency but also cost targets. can you spell those out?
[09:25] Priya: we want p50 under 250ms, p95 under 500ms ideally, and cost under $X per 1k requests — I'll confirm the exact dollar figure in a follow-up.
[09:45] Jenna: noted. we'll aim to hit p95 500ms with quantization and tuned batching.
[10:05] Liam: an operational ask — can we get token-level cost breakdown per route in the console? that helps us model spend.
[10:18] Samir: yes console shows token-level cost and latency per route, we'll share a short walkthrough.
[10:40] Priya: okay good. any blockers on our side?
[10:50] Liam: peering + firewall rules, I'll have a doc by EOD. also need a test KMS key.
[11:05] Marta: compliance asks — SOC2 evidence and encryption at rest detail.
[11:20] Samir: we'll send SOC2 summary and sample audit artifacts, and KMS integration guide.
[11:45] Jenna: back to results — one caveat, the baseline had some transcription mislabels for long contexts, we think it's a batching edge-case; we'll instrument KV cache hit rates and share logs.
[12:15] Priya: can you also run a long-context test with 2k token prompts? that's where we saw regressions.
[12:30] Jenna: yes we'll include a 2k token long-context run in the suite.
[13:05] Samir: ok who owns what? Jenna does the benchmark runs and will post results, Liam completes peering, Samir sends security docs, Priya finalizes success criteria.
[13:30] Priya: sounds good.
[14:00] Jenna: small tech detail — when enabling 8-bit quantization we recommend a warm-up sequence to populate KV cache; that reduces first request jitter.
[14:18] Liam: noted. how long is warm-up?
[14:25] Jenna: usually 3-5 requests per session depending on context length.
[15:00] Samir: any concerns about model variants? we suggested a 'compatible hosted fallback' which uses the same architecture but slightly smaller to preserve latency.
[15:18] Priya: we prefer no fallback to smaller model during pilot to keep evaluation apples-to-apples; we might enable fallback for production later.
[15:35] Samir: fine — we'll disable cross-pool fallback for the pilot.
[16:00] Jenna: I'll also attach the quant profile and the tuning script to the results sheet.
[16:20] Priya: great. one more compliance Q — does Redwood support customer-managed audit logging retention?
[16:34] Samir: yes retention policies are configurable, and we can export logs to your S3 if you want long-term retention.
[17:00] Marta: perfect, export to our S3 is preferred.
[17:12] Liam: timeline note — I'll aim to finalize peering by 2027-10-15, KMS key by 2027-10-14.
[17:30] Samir: Jenna — can you schedule the benchmark for 2027-10-18?
[17:40] Jenna: tentatively yes, we'll confirm after peering is done.
[18:05] Priya: ok if we hit p95 under 500ms with quantization and KV tuning then we can move to the next stage for an expanded pilot.
[18:22] Samir: perfect. last item — pricing ask: Priya asked for rough cost estimate for Dedicated throughput at target loads. Jenna will include an estimate in the results.
[18:40] Jenna: yes estimate included.
[19:05] Samir: any other blockers?
[19:12] Priya: none from me.
[19:25] Marta: none.
[19:40] Samir: cool — recap of next steps and I'll follow up with the security pack and calendar invite for 2027-10-19 10:00 PT to review. thanks all.
[19:58] (call ends)
Notes: audio had moderate WER in some long-context parts; speaker overlap around 04:00 and 11:00; names occasionally transcribed slightly off (e.g., 'NexaHead' vs NexaHead).
